To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucuronosyl‐, sulfotrans‐ and glutathione‐ S‐transferases are distributed heterogeneously across the liver acinus.
the activities of glucuronosulfotransferases, sulfotransfersases and glutathione transferases are heterogeneously distributed across the liver acinus.

glucuronosyl‐, glutathione‐, and sulfotransfearse activities are localized heterogenously across human liver lobules, with the former two enzymes being localized predominantly in periventral regions and sulfotransfersae in periportal areas, and that β‐glucoronidase and sulfotase activities are evenly distributed across the lobule, and that sulfation is more subject to futile cycling than glucuronidatin in human liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new methods for microdetermining transferase and hydrolase activities in microsomal fractions of liver tissue and with the use of these methods for the determination of sublobular distribution of enzymes associated with the formation and hydrolysis of glucuronide, glutathione and sulfate conjugates in human liver.

the development of methods and the determination of enzyme activities for the conjugation and deconjugation of xenobiotics and their metabolites in microdissect samples of periportal (zone 1) and pericentral (zone 3) regions of the liver lobules from human liver.
the distribution and regulation of enzymes associated with the formation and hydrolysis of sulfate, glucuronide, and glutathione‐conjugates in human liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sublobular distribution of glucuronidation is similar to that of glutathione conjugate formation, but that sulfation is predominantly periportal in origin.
sulfotransferases are predominantly located in periportal regions and that glucuronosyl- and glutathione‐S‐transferases are located predominantly in pericental regions.
the transferase activities are heterogeneously distributed across the liver, whereas the hydrolase activities are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucuronidation and glutathione‐conjugation are more important in the pericentral region, whereas sulfation and hydrolysis are more important in periportal regions.

the distribution of transferases across the liver lobules of human liver is consistent with a model in which the pericentral zone is specialized for the conjugation of lipophilic substrates with glutathione and the periportal zone is specialized for conjugation with glucuronate.
glucuronidation is predominantly a pericentral phenomenon, whereas sulfate conjugation occurs predominantly in periportal areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant differences in the activities of transferases and hydrolyses across the liver lobules and this should be taken into consideration when studying conjugating enzymes in the liver.
the distribution of conjugation enzymes in human liver is not as uniform as previously believed.

the distribution of transferase and hydrolase activities in human liver is heterogeneous, with the periportal region having a greater proportion of sulfotransferease activity than the pericentral region.
